key_insight: Predictive synthesis aims to move MOF and COF discovery from intuition-based trial-and-error toward AI/ML-guided, data-informed control of complex reaction conditions.
engineering_relevance: For materials engineers, this could shorten design-build-test cycles and improve the probability of obtaining targeted crystalline frameworks with fewer failed experiments.
method: Review the synthesis of MOFs and COFs as a multidimensional, interdependent parameter space.
Frame AI/ML as a way to recommend next experiments using prior knowledge and uncertainty.
Envision progression from static recipe prediction to real-time control and transferable formation principles.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a Perspective rather than a new benchmark study, so its support comes from conceptual synthesis of prior knowledge, experimental uncertainty, and observed failure modes instead of reported performance metrics.
watch_item: A key challenge is that predictive models may not transfer well across labs, chemistries, or changing experimental conditions without robust, standardized training data.
paper_title: Predictive Synthesis of MOFs and COFs
